handReconstructed.detail: motion is not installed. Surface renders the settled inline opacity:1 (opacity:0 for the bar-fade-initial fixture); the 0.275s ease fade itself is JS-driven and must be sampled by the parity runner.

Rendered settled: presence and layout groups render their children, a motion.div with an animate target carries it as inline style (App reveal: width:auto;opacity:1), the workspace indicator (layoutId, no animate) keeps its own style. The app reveal/exit (width 0<->auto, opacity 0<->1, duration max(0.15, length*0.15/15) s, legacy ease) and the indicator layout spring (bounce 0, duration motionRaw.durationSlower) are JS-driven and sampled by the parity runner against models built from the pinned constants.
Error boundaries do not run in static rendering. The global-error fixture renders the pinned QueryErrorFallback directly; the boundary wrapper has no DOM of its own.
start/end/distance come from layout measurement in a browser. The *-scrolling fixtures inject fixed values into the pinned component through a useState shim; the parity runner measures real values.
loadedArtwork is set by an Image() load effect. Fixtures inject the loaded (data URI) and failed (null) results. Artwork pixels are a synthetic generated PNG, not captured media.

React Query, Tauri invoke/events, the useTauri/useWidgetToggle/useMediaQuery hooks and the Weather store plumbing are replaced by fixture data (stubs.ts). Labels, colors, icon choice and markup are computed by the pinned sources.

The pinned Spaces.state.ts runs: fetchWorkspacesData/fetchAppsData sort and map synthetic invoke answers (get_tiling_*; rejected when the scenario has no Tiling) and useSpaces derives display names, the 40/25 truncation and the laptop focused-only reduction. Only its I/O is replaced: useSuspenseQuery returns the fetchers' resolved results (or suspends for spaces-fallback), useMediaQuery is the fixture breakpoint, Tauri events are inert, and isEnabled (useState(false), set by is_tiling_enabled/INITIALIZED in effects) is the fixture's enabled flag. The App/AppList/Workspace/WorkspaceList components, constants and styles run pinned.

handReconstructed.detail: orchestrator decision 2026-11-10, reported to user: legacy Workspace passes workspaceIcons[name] = undefined to Icon for a name outside the map and the Bar is lost to the error fallback. For the Workspace.tsx importer only, Icon renders nothing when icon is undefined, so the pinned Workspace draws its button and indicator without an icon.

user decision 2026-11-10: the strip's @hugeicons/core-free-icons glyphs come from 4.4.0 (the repository version; integrity from the repository bun.lock), not legacy 4.2.3. @hugeicons/react stays at the legacy 1.1.9 and simple-icons at 13.15.1. Glyphs changed since 4.2.3 are listed in stripIcons.glyphChangesFrom4_2_3.

Linaria is replaced by a template-collecting css/cx stub and a small flattener (css.ts). Stylis vendor-prefix duplicates are not generated. Class names are generated (lr-<Module>-<name>). Rule order follows legacy module evaluation order, which is how the legacy bundle ordered its CSS.
The legacy formatter runs unchanged against a frozen Date in UTC.
Rendered with the repository react-dom/server (classic JSX transform); the legacy lockfile pins react 19.2.8.
